# Risk model backtest [SYNTHETIC: a known-truth history from sample_data/generate_risk_panel.py, 220 invented customers]

Model settings version `2026-11-26.1`; renewals judged from 180 days out; events: churned, downsold.

Scored out of time: 364 renewals, 64 of them lost (base rate 17.6%), from 7639 snapshots (2024-11-04 to 2026-08-24). Each renewal is judged 150, 90, 30 days ahead (900 judgements). Intervals are 95%, from resampling whole customers.

| Method | AUC | 95% interval | Precision, top 10% | Recall, top 10% | Brier | Losses expected / seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| scorecard (100 - health) | 0.767 | 0.700 to 0.834 | 0.456 | 0.293 | - | - |
| expert prior (probability) | 0.766 | 0.698 to 0.832 | 0.456 | 0.293 | 0.113 | 138 / 140 |
| trained model (probability) | 0.768 | 0.705 to 0.833 | 0.444 | 0.286 | 0.113 | 145 / 140 |

Trained model minus expert prior, AUC: -0.006 to 0.010 (95% interval). The trained model is worth adopting only when this interval sits above zero and its Brier score is lower.

**The rules alone** (a hard red or health under 50) flag 0.114 of judgements, with precision 0.427 and recall 0.314 (AUC 0.618).

**Only the periods where the model had learned something** (747 judgements, 120 lost): AUC 0.759 against the prior's 0.754; Brier 0.118 against 0.118.

Retrainings by stage: prior 3, calibrated 13, dimension 8. The last one had 72 renewals lost to learn from.
